title.zh: 卷505 列傳二百九十二 艺術四
title.raw: 卷505 列傳二百九十二 艺術四

sentences.zh: 王來咸褚士寶馮行貞甘鳳池曹竹齋潘佩言

translations.literal: Wang Laixian; Chu Shibao; Feng Xingzhen; Gan Fengchi; Cao Zhuzhai; Pan Peiyan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Laixian, Chu Shibao, Feng Xingzhen, Gan Fengchi, Cao Zhuzhai, and Pan Peiyan.

sentences.zh: 江之桐梁九張漣葉陶劉源唐英戴梓

translations.literal: Jiang Zhitong; Liang Jiu; Zhang Lian; Ye Tao; Liu Yuan; Tang Ying; Dai Zi.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zhitong, Liang Jiu, Zhang Lian, Ye Tao, Liu Yuan, Tang Ying, and Dai Zi.

sentences.zh: 丁守存徐壽子建寅華封

translations.literal: Ding Shoucun; Xu Shou; Zi Jianyin; Hua Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Shoucun, Xu Shou, Zi Jianyin, and Hua Feng.

sentences.zh: 王來咸，字征南，浙江鄞縣人。

translations.literal: Wang Laixian, styled Zhengnan, was a man of Yin County in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Laixian, whose style name was Zhengnan, came from Yin County in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 先世居奉化，自祖父居鄞，至來咸徙同，從同里單思南受內家拳法。

translations.literal: His forebears dwelt in Fenghua; from his grandfather's generation they lived in Yin; when Laixian came of age he moved to Tonggu and received inner-school boxing methods from his fellow townsman Shan Sinan.
translations.idiomatic: His family had originally lived in Fenghua; from his grandfather's day they settled in Yin, and Laixian later moved to Tonggu, where he studied inner-school boxing under his neighbor Shan Sinan.

sentences.zh: 內家者，起於宋武當道士張三峰，其法以靜制動，應手即僕，與少林之主於搏人者異，故別少林為外家。

translations.literal: Inner-school boxing arose from the Song Wudang Daoist Zhang Sanfeng; its method uses stillness to overcome movement, and at a touch the opponent falls — unlike Shaolin, which chiefly aims at striking others down, so Shaolin was set apart as the outer school.
translations.idiomatic: The inner school began with the Wudang Daoist Zhang Sanfeng in the Song. Its art counters motion with stillness: one touch and the opponent goes down. Shaolin, by contrast, is built around overpowering an adversary, and so came to be called the outer school.

sentences.zh: 其後流傳於秦、晉間，至明中葉，王宗岳為最著，溫州、陳州同受之，遂流傳於溫州。

translations.literal: Afterward it spread through Qin and Jin; by mid-Ming Wang Zongyue was most prominent; Wenzhou and Chenzhou both received it, and so it spread to Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The art later spread through the Qin and Jin regions. By the mid-Ming, Wang Zongyue was its most celebrated master; Wenzhou and Chenzhou both inherited the tradition, and from there it passed into Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖間，張松溪最著，松溪之徒三四人，寧波葉繼美為魁，遂流傳於寧波。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing reign Zhang Songxi was most prominent; Songxi had three or four disciples, and Ye Jimei of Ningbo was foremost, and so it spread to Ningbo.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiajing era Zhang Songxi stood at the head of the art. He had three or four disciples; Ye Jimei of Ningbo was the leading one, and the lineage thereafter took root in Ningbo.

sentences.zh: 得繼美之傳者，曰吳崑山、周雲泉、陳貞石、孫繼槎及思南，各有授受。

translations.literal: Those who received Jimei's transmission were Wu Kunshan, Zhou Yunquan, Chen Zhenshi, Sun Jiqiao, and Sinan — each with his own line of teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Jimei's disciples included Wu Kunshan, Zhou Yunquan, Chen Zhenshi, Sun Jiqiao, and Sinan, each passing the art on in his own way.

sentences.zh: 思南從征關白，歸老於家，以術教，頗惜其精微。

translations.literal: Sinan campaigned against the Japanese invader Hideyoshi, retired in old age at home, taught the art, and was rather sparing with its subtle refinements.
translations.idiomatic: Sinan had served in the campaign against the Japanese invader Hideyoshi. In old age he retired home to teach, but he guarded the art's finer points closely.

sentences.zh: 來咸從樓上穴板窺之，得其梗概。

translations.literal: Laixian spied through a hole bored in the upstairs floorboard and grasped the general outline.
translations.idiomatic: Laixian bored a hole in the floor above and watched through it until he had grasped the gist of the training.

sentences.zh: 以銀卮易美檟奉思南，始盡以不傳者傳之。

translations.literal: He exchanged a silver goblet for fine coffin wood to present to Sinan, and only then was the whole of what had been withheld transmitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: He traded a silver cup for fine coffin wood and offered it to Sinan as a gift; only then did Sinan teach him everything he had held back.

sentences.zh: 來咸為人機警，不露圭角，非遇甚困不發。

translations.literal: Laixian was quick-witted by nature, showed no sharp edge, and would not act unless pressed to extremity.
translations.idiomatic: Laixian was sharp and alert by nature, never flaunting his skill, and he would not unleash it except under great provocation.

sentences.zh: 凡搏人皆以其穴，死穴、暈穴、啞穴，一切如銅人圖法。

translations.literal: Whenever he struck down opponents he targeted their points — death points, fainting points, mute points — all according to the bronze-figure chart method.
translations.idiomatic: In combat he always aimed at the vital points — death points, fainting points, mute points — following the method of the bronze acufigure chart.

sentences.zh: 有惡少侮之，為所擊，數日不溺，謝過，乃得如故。

translations.literal: A rowdy youth insulted him; struck by Laixian, for several days he could not urinate; after apologizing, he was restored as before.
translations.idiomatic: Once a bully mocked him; Laixian struck him, and for days the man could not pass water. Only after he apologized was he restored to normal.

sentences.zh: 牧童竊學其法，擊伴侶，立死。

translations.literal: A herd boy secretly learned his method, struck a companion, and the companion died at once.
translations.idiomatic: A shepherd boy secretly picked up his technique, struck a playmate, and the boy dropped dead on the spot.

sentences.zh: 視之，曰：「此暈穴。」

translations.literal: Laixian looked and said: "This is a fainting point."
translations.idiomatic: Laixian examined him and said, "That was a fainting point."

sentences.zh: 不久果甦。

translations.literal: Before long the boy indeed revived.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the boy did indeed come round.

sentences.zh: 任俠，嘗為人報仇，有致金以讎其弟者，絕之，曰：「此以禽獸待我也！」

translations.literal: He was chivalrous; once when someone offered him gold to avenge a brother, he refused, saying: "You treat me like a beast!"
translations.idiomatic: He lived by the code of the knight-errant. Once a man offered him gold to avenge a brother; he refused, saying, "You would have me behave like an animal!"

sentences.zh: 明末，嘗入伍為把總，從錢肅樂起兵浙東，事敗，隱居於家。

translations.literal: At the end of the Ming he once joined the army as a platoon commander, followed Qian Zhile in raising troops in eastern Zhejiang; when the cause failed he lived in seclusion at home.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Ming he served as a platoon commander and joined Qian Zhile's uprising in eastern Zhejiang. When the cause failed, he withdrew into seclusion.

sentences.zh: 慕其藝者，多通殷勤，皆不顧。

translations.literal: Many who admired his art sought to win his favor — he paid none of them heed.
translations.idiomatic: Many who admired his skill tried to court him with favors; he ignored them all.

sentences.zh: 鋤地擔糞，安於食貧。

translations.literal: He hoed fields and carried night soil, content in poverty.
translations.idiomatic: He hoed the earth and carried night soil, content to live in poverty.

sentences.zh: 未嘗讀書，與士大夫談論蘊藉，不知為粗人。

translations.literal: Though he had never studied books, in conversation with scholar-officials he was refined and restrained — one would not know he was a rough man.
translations.idiomatic: He had never read books, yet in talk with scholar-officials he was polished and restrained; no one would have guessed he was a rough man.

sentences.zh: 黃宗羲與之遊，同入天童，僧少焰有膂力，四五人不能掣其手，稍近來咸，蹶然負痛。

translations.literal: Huang Zongxi traveled with him; together they entered Tiantong Monastery. The monk Shaoyan had great physical strength — four or five men could not pull his hand free; when he came slightly near Laixian, he suddenly collapsed in pain.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zongxi often kept his company. Once they entered Tiantong Monastery together. The monk Shaoyan was immensely strong — four or five men together could not wrest his hand loose — yet when he drew a little near Laixian, he suddenly crumpled in pain.

sentences.zh: 來咸嘗曰：「今人以內家無可炫耀，於是以外家羼之，此學行衰矣！」

translations.literal: Laixian once said: "People today find inner-school boxing offers nothing to show off, so they mix in outer-school methods — the tradition is in decline!"
translations.idiomatic: Laixian once said, "People today think inner-school boxing has nothing flashy to display, so they adulterate it with outer-school techniques. The art is dying!"

sentences.zh: 因為宗羲論述其學源流。

translations.literal: Thereupon he expounded for Zongxi the origins and transmission of the art.
translations.idiomatic: He then laid out for Zongxi the origins and transmission of the school.

sentences.zh: 康熙八年，卒，年五十三。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Kangxi he died, aged fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth year of the Kangxi reign, at the age of fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 宗羲子百家從之學，演其說為內家拳法一卷，百家後無所傳焉。

translations.literal: Zongxi's son Baijia studied under him and elaborated his teachings into one fascicle on inner-school boxing method; afterward Baijia had no one to transmit it further.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zongxi's son Baijia studied under him and expanded his teachings into a one-volume Inner-School Boxing Method; afterward the lineage died with Baijia.

sentences.zh: 清中葉，河北有太極拳，云其法出於山西王宗岳，其法式論解，與百家之言相出入。

translations.literal: In mid-Qing Hebei had taiji boxing, said to derive its method from Wang Zongyue of Shanxi; its form theory and explication diverged in places from Baijia's statements.
translations.idiomatic: In the mid-Qing, taiji boxing appeared in Hebei, said to descend from Wang Zongyue of Shanxi. Its formal theory and commentary partly agreed and partly disagreed with Baijia's account.

sentences.zh: 至清末，傳習者頗眾雲。

translations.literal: By the late Qing those who practiced and transmitted it were quite numerous, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: By the late Qing, it is said, those who practiced and passed it on had grown quite numerous.

sentences.zh: 褚士寶，字復生，江南上海人。

translations.literal: Chu Shibao, styled Fusheng, was a man of Shanghai in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Shibao, whose style name was Fusheng, came from Shanghai in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 家素封，膂力過人，好技擊，遊學四方。

translations.literal: His family had long been wealthy; his physical strength surpassed others'; he loved martial combat and traveled to study everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Born into a wealthy family, he possessed extraordinary strength, loved the martial arts, and wandered far and wide to study them.

sentences.zh: 與畢昆陽、武君卿為友，遂精槍法，名曰四平槍，旋轉如風，人莫能近。

translations.literal: He befriended Bi Kunyang and Wu Junqing, and thus became expert in spear method called Four-Square Spear — whirling like wind, none could approach him.
translations.idiomatic: Through friendship with Bi Kunyang and Wu Junqing he mastered a spear art called the Four-Square Spear. It spun like a whirlwind; no one could get near him.

sentences.zh: 同邑有張擎者，虎頸板肋，力舉百鈞，橫行為閭里患，眾請士寶除之。

translations.literal: In the same district was one Zhang Qing, with a tiger's neck and iron ribs, strength to lift a hundred jun — he swaggered about and was a scourge to the neighborhood; the crowd asked Shibao to eliminate him.
translations.idiomatic: In the same county lived Zhang Qing, bull-necked and barrel-chested, able to lift a hundred jun. He terrorized the neighborhood, and the people begged Shibao to remove him.

sentences.zh: 同飲酒，擎自誇其勇，酒酣，攘臂作勢，士寶徐以箸點其胸，曰：「子盍坐而言乎？」

translations.literal: Drinking together, Qing boastfully vaunted his bravery; when deep in wine he rolled up his sleeves and struck a pose — Shibao gently touched his chest with chopsticks and said: "Why not sit down and speak?"
translations.idiomatic: They drank together. Qing bragged of his courage; when he was well into his cups he rolled up his sleeves and squared up. Shibao lightly tapped his chest with chopsticks and said, "Why not sit down and talk?"

sentences.zh: 擎遂默然，少頃辭去，越日，死於橋亭。

translations.literal: Qing then fell silent; shortly he took his leave; the next day he died at a bridge pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Qing fell silent at once. Soon he excused himself and left; the next day he was found dead at a bridge pavilion.

sentences.zh: 明季福王南渡，兵部員外郎何剛薦士寶為伏波營游擊。

translations.literal: In the late Ming when the Prince of Fu crossed south, Bureau of War Assistant Department Director He Gang recommended Shibao as mobile commander of the Fubo Camp.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Fu fled south in the late Ming, He Gang of the Bureau of War recommended Shibao for the post of mobile commander in the Fubo Camp.

sentences.zh: 未之官，南​​都陷，終老於家。

translations.literal: Before he took office the Southern Capital fell; he spent his old age at home.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the appointment, the Southern Capital fell, and he lived out his days at home.

sentences.zh: 所傳弟子有王聖蕃、池天榮。

translations.literal: Among disciples he transmitted to were Wang Shengfan and Chi Tianrong.
translations.idiomatic: Among his disciples were Wang Shengfan and Chi Tianrong.

sentences.zh: 天榮又傳浙江提督喬照。

translations.literal: Tianrong in turn transmitted to Zhejiang Provincial Military Commander Qiao Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Tianrong in turn passed the art to Qiao Zhao, provincial military commander of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 其槍譜二種及治傷藥酒方，世猶有藏之者。

translations.literal: Two kinds of his spear manual and medicinal wine formulas for treating wounds — the world still has collectors of them.
translations.idiomatic: Two versions of his spear manual and his medicinal wine recipes for treating wounds are still preserved by collectors.

sentences.zh: 馮行貞，字服之，江南常熟人。

translations.literal: Feng Xingzhen, styled Fuzhi, was a man of Changshu in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Xingzhen, whose style name was Fuzhi, came from Changshu in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 父班，以文學者。

translations.literal: His father Ban was known for literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ban was a scholar of literary accomplishment.

sentences.zh: 兄行賢，傳其學。

translations.literal: His elder brother Xingxian inherited that learning.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Xingxian carried on that scholarly tradition.

sentences.zh: 行貞少亦喜讀書，工小詞，性倜儻不羈。

translations.literal: In youth Xingzhen also loved reading, was skilled at short lyric poetry, and by nature was free-spirited and unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Xingzhen also loved books and wrote short lyric poems with skill. By nature he was bold and untamed.

sentences.zh: 善射，能以後矢落前矢，投石子於百步外無不中。

translations.literal: He was skilled at archery — could knock down the front arrow with a rear arrow; throwing stones a hundred paces none missed.
translations.idiomatic: He was a fine archer: he could split the leading arrow with the one that followed. Stones he hurled a hundred paces away never missed their mark.

sentences.zh: 實雞卵殼以礦灰，遇劇盜，輒先發雞卵中其目。

translations.literal: He filled eggshells with mineral lime; encountering fierce bandits he would first launch an egg to hit their eyes.
translations.idiomatic: He packed eggshells with mineral lime; when he met fierce bandits he would first hurl an egg into their eyes.

sentences.zh: 山東響馬老瓜賊為行旅患，聞馮氏名，莫敢攖。

translations.literal: The Shandong mounted bandit nicknamed Old Melon Thief plagued travelers; hearing the Feng name, none dared provoke him.
translations.idiomatic: The Shandong highwayman known as Old Melon Thief preyed on travelers, yet even he, hearing the Feng name, did not dare pick a fight.

sentences.zh: 從休寧程打虎及張老受槍法，馳突無敵。

translations.literal: Following Cheng Dahu of Xiuning and Old Zhang he received spear method; charging and thrusting, none could match him.
translations.idiomatic: He studied spear fighting under Cheng Dahu of Xiuning and Old Zhang. In the charge and the thrust he had no equal.

sentences.zh: 山行遇虎，以短槍斃之。

translations.literal: Traveling in the mountains he met a tiger and killed it with a short spear.
translations.idiomatic: Once, traveling in the hills, he met a tiger and killed it with a short spear.

sentences.zh: 嘗為客報仇。

translations.literal: He once avenged a client.
translations.idiomatic: He once took a client's revenge.

sentences.zh: 康熙中，從康親王杰書軍南征，有功，當得官，尋棄歸。

translations.literal: In the Kangxi reign he followed Prince Kang Jieshu's army on the southern campaign, merited reward and was due for office — soon he abandoned it and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kangxi reign he marched south with Prince Kang Jieshu's army, earned distinction, and was offered an official post — but he soon gave it up and went home.

sentences.zh: 僑居吳中婁門外村落，以經書教授，詩畫自娛。

translations.literal: He lived as a sojourner in a village outside Lou Gate in Suzhou, teaching the classics, amusing himself with poetry and painting.
translations.idiomatic: He settled in a village beyond Lou Gate in Suzhou, taught the classics for a living, and passed his days in poetry and painting.

sentences.zh: 年七十餘，卒。

translations.literal: In his seventies he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in his seventies.

sentences.zh: 以槍法授同縣陶元淳，元淳後無傳者。

translations.literal: He transmitted spear method to his fellow townsman Tao Yuanchun; afterward Yuanchun had no one to transmit it further.
translations.idiomatic: He taught his spear art to his fellow townsman Tao Yuanchun, but the lineage ended with Yuanchun.

sentences.zh: 甘鳳池，江南江寧人。

translations.literal: Gan Fengchi was a man of Jiangning in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Fengchi came from Jiangning in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 少以勇聞。

translations.literal: In youth he was known for courage.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was famed for his courage.

sentences.zh: 康熙中，客京師貴邸。

translations.literal: In the Kangxi reign he sojourned at the residence of a noble in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kangxi reign he lodged as a guest in the house of a great family in the capital.

sentences.zh: 力士張大義者慕其名，自濟南來見。

translations.literal: The strongman Zhang Dayi admired his reputation and came from Jinan to see him.
translations.idiomatic: A brawler named Zhang Dayi, who admired his reputation, traveled from Jinan to meet him.

sentences.zh: 酒酣，命與鳳池角，鳳池辭，固強之。

translations.literal: When deep in wine he ordered a wrestling match with Fengchi; Fengchi declined but was forcibly pressed to it.
translations.idiomatic: When the wine was flowing, Dayi demanded a bout with Fengchi. Fengchi refused, but Dayi would not take no for an answer.

sentences.zh: 大義身長八尺餘，脛力強大，以鐵裹拇，騰躍若風雨之驟至。

translations.literal: Dayi was over eight chi tall, with tremendously powerful shins; iron wrapped his thumbs; he leaped like a sudden storm.
translations.idiomatic: Dayi stood more than eight chi tall, with shins of iron strength. He bound his thumbs in metal and leaped like a sudden storm.

sentences.zh: 鳳池卻立倚柱，俟其來，承以手，大義大呼僕，血滿鞾，解視，拇盡嵌鐵中。

translations.literal: Fengchi stood back against a pillar, waited for him to come, and received him with his hands; Dayi cried out and fell — blood filled his boots; when unwrapped, his thumbs were embedded in the iron.
translations.idiomatic: Fengchi stepped back to lean against a pillar, waited for the rush, and caught him with his hands. Dayi cried out and collapsed; blood filled his boots. When the wrappings were removed, his thumbs were driven deep into the iron.

sentences.zh: 即墨馬玉麟，長軀大腹，以帛約身，緣牆升木，捷於猱。

translations.literal: Ma Yulin of Jimo had a long frame and great belly; binding his body with cloth he scaled walls and trees, swifter than a monkey.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yulin of Jimo was long-limbed and big-bellied. Wrapping cloth tight around his body, he could climb walls and trees faster than a monkey.

sentences.zh: 客揚州巨賈家，鳳池後至，居其上。

translations.literal: Staying as guest at a great merchant's house in Yangzhou, Fengchi arrived later and was lodged above him.
translations.idiomatic: Both were guests at a wealthy merchant's house in Yangzhou. Fengchi arrived later and was given the better room above Yulin.

sentences.zh: 玉麟不平，與角技，終日無勝負。

translations.literal: Yulin resented this; they contended in skill — all day with no victor.
translations.idiomatic: Yulin took offense. They matched skills all day long, and neither could prevail.

sentences.zh: 鳳池曰：「此勁敵，非張大義比！」

translations.literal: Fengchi said: "This is a formidable foe — no comparison to Zhang Dayi!"
translations.idiomatic: Fengchi said, "This is a real opponent — nothing like Zhang Dayi!"

sentences.zh: 明日又角，數蹈其瑕，玉麟直前擒鳳池，以駢指卻之，玉麟僕地，慚遁。

translations.literal: The next day they wrestled again; several times Fengchi exploited his flaws; Yulin rushed forward to seize Fengchi; Fengchi repelled him with the parallel-finger technique; Yulin fell to the ground and fled in shame.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they fought again. Several times Fengchi found openings in Yulin's guard. Yulin lunged to grab him; Fengchi turned him back with the parallel-finger technique. Yulin fell to the ground and fled in shame.

sentences.zh: 鳳池嘗語人曰：「吾力不逾中人，所以能勝人者，善藉其力以製之耳。」

translations.literal: Fengchi once told people: "My strength does not exceed that of an ordinary man; what enables me to overcome others is skill at borrowing their force to control them."
translations.idiomatic: Fengchi once told people, "My strength is no greater than an ordinary man's. I win because I know how to borrow an opponent's force and turn it against him."

sentences.zh: 手能破堅，握鉛錫化為水。

translations.literal: His hands could break the hard; gripping lead and tin he could melt them into water.
translations.idiomatic: His hands could shatter hard objects; when he gripped lead or tin it melted in his grasp like water.

sentences.zh: 又善導引術，同里譚氏子病瘵，醫不效，鳳池於靜室窒牖戶，夜與合背坐，四十九日而痊。

translations.literal: He was also skilled in daoyin exercises; a Tan family son in his neighborhood had consumption — medicine failed; Fengchi in a quiet room blocked windows and doors, sat back-to-back with him by night — after forty-nine days he recovered.
translations.idiomatic: He was also adept at daoyin exercises. A neighbor's son in the Tan family had consumption; doctors could not cure him. Fengchi sealed the windows and doors of a quiet room and sat back-to-back with the boy through the nights; after forty-nine days the boy recovered.

sentences.zh: 喜任俠，接人和易，見者不知為賁、育。

translations.literal: He delighted in chivalry, received people with easy warmth — those who met him did not know he was a Ben or Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He loved the life of the knight-errant and treated everyone with easy warmth. Those who met him never guessed he was another Ben or Yu.

sentences.zh: 雍正中，浙江總督李衛捕治江寧顧云如邪術不軌獄，株連百數十人，鳳池亦被逮，讞擬大辟。

translations.literal: In the Yongzheng reign Zhejiang Governor-General Li Wei arrested and tried the case of Gu Yunru of Jiangning for heterodox arts and seditious conduct, implicating over a hundred people; Fengchi was also seized and the verdict proposed capital punishment.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongzheng reign, Zhejiang governor-general Li Wei prosecuted Gu Yunru of Jiangning for heterodox arts and seditious plotting; more than a hundred people were implicated. Fengchi was arrested too, and the sentence proposed was death.

sentences.zh: 世宗於此獄從寬，未盡駢誅。

translations.literal: The Yongzheng Emperor showed leniency in this case and did not carry out wholesale execution.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongzheng Emperor showed mercy in the affair and did not execute the whole lot.

sentences.zh: 或云鳳池年八十餘，終於家。

translations.literal: Some say Fengchi lived to over eighty and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Some say Fengchi lived past eighty and died at home.

sentences.zh: 江湖間流傳其佚事多荒誕，著其可信者。

translations.literal: Among the jianghu world many absurd tales of him circulate; here only the believable ones are recorded.
translations.idiomatic: The rivers-and-lakes world is full of wild stories about him; only those that seem credible are set down here.

sentences.zh: 曹竹齋，以字行，佚其名，福建人。

translations.literal: Cao Zhuzhai, known by his courtesy name — his personal name is lost — was a man of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhuzhai, known only by his courtesy name — his given name is lost — came from Fujian.

sentences.zh: 老而貧，賣卜揚州市。

translations.literal: Old and poor, he sold divinations in Yangzhou city.
translations.idiomatic: Old and poor, he made a living casting fortunes in Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 江、淮間健者，莫能當其一拳，故稱曹一拳。

translations.literal: Strongmen between the Yangtze and Huai — none could withstand one punch of his; hence he was called Cao One-Fist.
translations.idiomatic: Among the strongmen of the Yangtze-Huai region, none could take a single punch from him, and so he was called Cao One-Fist.

sentences.zh: 少年以重幣請其術，不可。

translations.literal: A youth offered rich payment to request his art — he would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: A young man offered a large sum to learn his art, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 或怪之，則曰：「此皆無賴子，豈當授藝以助虐哉？

translations.literal: When someone questioned this he said: "These are all worthless ruffians — how should one teach martial arts to help them tyrannize others?
translations.idiomatic: When someone wondered at this, he said, "They are nothing but worthless ruffians. Why should I teach them fighting so they can bully others?

sentences.zh: 拳棒，古先舞蹈之遺也，君子習之，所以調血脈，養壽命，其粗乃以御侮。

translations.literal: Fist and staff are vestiges of ancient ritual dance; the gentleman practices them to regulate blood and vessels and nurture life — in their crude form they serve to repel insult.
translations.idiomatic: Boxing and the staff are relics of the ancient ritual dances. A gentleman trains in them to harmonize the blood and breath and prolong life; in their rougher form they serve only to ward off insult.

sentences.zh: 必彼侮而我御之，若以之侮人，則反為人所禦而自敗矣。

translations.literal: It must be that they insult and I repel; if one uses them to insult others, one in turn is repelled by others and defeats oneself.
translations.idiomatic: The proper use is to answer insult with defense. Use them to insult others, and others will turn them back on you — you defeat yourself.

sentences.zh: 無賴子以血氣事侵凌，其氣浮於上，而立腳虛，故因其奔赴之勢，略藉手而僕耳。

translations.literal: Ruffians rely on hot blood to bully — their qi floats upward while their footing is empty; therefore by their rushing momentum, a slight touch of the hand brings them down.
translations.idiomatic: Ruffians bully with hot blood alone. Their energy rides high while their footing is hollow; ride their rush, and the lightest touch of the hand brings them down.

sentences.zh: 一身止兩拳，拳之大才數寸，焉足衛五尺之軀，且以接四面乎？

translations.literal: The body has only two fists; a fist at largest is a few inches — how can it guard a five-chi body and receive attacks from all four sides?
translations.idiomatic: The body has only two fists, and each fist spans at most a few inches. How can that guard a five-chi frame against blows from every direction?

sentences.zh: 惟養吾正氣，使周於吾身，彼之手足近吾身，而吾之拳，即在其所近之處。

translations.literal: Only nurture my upright qi so it pervades my body — when their hands and feet approach my body, my fist is precisely where they approach.
translations.idiomatic: Cultivate upright qi until it fills the whole body. When an enemy's hands or feet come near, your fist is already where they arrive.

sentences.zh: 以彼虛囂之氣，與吾靜定之氣接，則自無幸矣。

translations.literal: When their empty clamorous qi meets my quiet settled qi, naturally they cannot succeed.
translations.idiomatic: When their hollow, blustering force meets your calm, rooted breath, they cannot prevail.

sentences.zh: 故至精是術者，其徵有二：一則精神貫注，而腹背皆乾滑如臘肉；

translations.literal: Therefore those who reach the utmost refinement in this art have two signs: one, spirit concentrated throughout, abdomen and back all dry and smooth like cured meat;
translations.idiomatic: Those who reach the highest mastery show two signs. First, the spirit is gathered throughout the body, and the abdomen and back are dry and smooth as cured meat;

sentences.zh: 一則氣體健舉，而額顱皆肥澤如粉粢。

translations.literal: one, breath vigorous and lifted, forehead and skull all plump and glossy like powdered millet cakes.
translations.idiomatic: second, the breath is strong and lifted, and the brow and crown are full and lustrous as fresh rice cakes.

sentences.zh: 是皆血脈流行，應乎自然，內充實而外和平，犯而不校者也。」

translations.literal: These all mean blood and vessels flowing, responding to nature — full within, peaceful without: struck yet not contending."
translations.idiomatic: Both mean the blood and breath move freely in accord with nature — firm within, serene without, struck yet unprovoked."

sentences.zh: 嘉慶末，歿於揚州，年八十餘。

translations.literal: Late in the Jiaqing reign he died in Yangzhou, aged over eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Yangzhou late in the Jiaqing reign, aged over eighty.

sentences.zh: 潘佩言，亦以字行，安徽歙縣人。

translations.literal: Pan Peiyan, also known by his courtesy name, was a man of She County in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Peiyan, known by his courtesy name, came from She County in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 以槍法著稱，稱潘五先生。

translations.literal: He was renowned for spear method and was called Master Pan Five.
translations.idiomatic: He was famed for spear fighting and was known as Master Pan Five.

sentences.zh: 其言：「槍長九尺，而桿圓四五寸，然槍入手，則全身悉委於桿。

translations.literal: His saying: "The spear is nine chi long while the shaft is four or five inches round, yet once the spear enters the hand the whole body entrusts itself to the shaft.
translations.idiomatic: He taught: "The spear is nine chi long and the shaft four or five inches thick, yet once it is in your hands the whole body commits itself to the shaft.

sentences.zh: 故必以小腹貼桿，使主運；

translations.literal: Therefore the lower abdomen must press the shaft and make it the master of motion;
translations.idiomatic: Press the lower abdomen to the shaft and let it drive the movement;

sentences.zh: 後手必盡錞，以虎口實擫之；

translations.literal: the rear hand must extend fully, with the tiger's mouth gripping firmly;
translations.idiomatic: the rear hand must reach its full extension, the web of the thumb gripping tight;

sentences.zh: 前手必直，令盡勢。

translations.literal: the front hand must be straight to release full power.
translations.idiomatic: the front hand must stay straight to release the full force.

sentences.zh: 以其掌根與後手虎口反正擰絞，而虛指使主導。

translations.literal: With the palm root and rear-hand tiger's mouth counter-twisting against each other, the flexible fingers serve as chief guide.
translations.idiomatic: Twist palm root and rear-hand grip against each other, and let the relaxed fingers lead the way.

sentences.zh: 兩足亦左虛右實，進退相任以趨勢。

translations.literal: The two feet too are left empty and right solid, advance and retreat mutually bearing the momentum.
translations.idiomatic: The feet too are left empty and right full, advance and retreat sharing the momentum between them.

sentences.zh: 使槍尖、前手尖、前足尖、鼻尖五尖相對，而五尺之身，自託廕於數寸之桿，遮閉周匝，敵仗無從入犯矣。

translations.literal: Align spear tip, front-hand tip, front-foot tip, and nose tip — the five points facing one another — and a five-chi body rests under the shelter of a few inches of shaft, closing all around so the enemy's weapon cannot enter.
translations.idiomatic: Line up spear tip, front-hand tip, front-foot tip, and nose tip — the five points facing one another — and a five-chi body shelters itself behind a shaft of a few inches, closing every angle so no enemy weapon can break through.

sentences.zh: 其用，有戳、有打；

translations.literal: In application there is thrusting and striking;
translations.idiomatic: In use there are thrusts and strikes;

sentences.zh: 其法，曰二、曰叉。

translations.literal: Its methods are called Two and Cross.
translations.idiomatic: In technique there are two forms, called the Two and the Cross.

sentences.zh: 二以取人，叉以拒人。

translations.literal: Two is used to take a man; Cross is used to repel a man.
translations.idiomatic: The Two is for striking an opponent; the Cross is for warding him off.

sentences.zh: 此叉則彼二，此二則彼叉。

translations.literal: When this side uses Cross, that side uses Two; when this side uses Two, that side uses Cross.
translations.idiomatic: When you Cross, your opponent Twoes; when you Two, he Crosses.

sentences.zh: 叉二循環，兩槍尖交如繞指，分寸間，出入百合，不得令相附。

translations.literal: Cross and Two cycle in alternation; the two spear tips interweave like fingers laced together. Within a space of inches they clash a hundred times in succession, yet the shafts must never be allowed to touch.
translations.idiomatic: Cross and Two alternate in endless cycle, the spear tips weaving together like interlaced fingers. Within inches they exchange a hundred blows, yet the shafts must never meet.

sentences.zh: 桿一附，則有僕者，故曰'千金難買一聲響'。

translations.literal: Once the shafts touch, someone falls—hence the saying, 'No amount of gold can buy a single clash of sound.'
translations.idiomatic: Let the shafts touch and someone goes down—hence the saying: 'A thousand ounces of gold cannot buy the sound of one clean clash.'

sentences.zh: 手同則爭目，目同則爭氣。

translations.literal: When the hands move alike, the contest shifts to the eyes; when the eyes lock, the contest shifts to the breath.
translations.idiomatic: When both hands move the same way, victory is decided by the eyes; when the eyes meet, it is decided by the breath.

sentences.zh: 氣之運也，久暫稍殊，而勝敗分焉。

translations.literal: In the circulation of breath, a slight difference in duration decides victory and defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Breath moves in its own rhythm; the slightest difference in endurance decides who wins and who loses.

sentences.zh: 故其術為至靜。」

translations.literal: Therefore this art reaches its perfection in stillness."
translations.idiomatic: That is why this art finds its highest expression in utter stillness."

sentences.zh: 「吾授徒百數，而莫能傳吾術。

translations.literal: I have taught disciples numbering in the hundreds, yet none has been able to transmit my art.
translations.idiomatic: I have taught hundreds of disciples, yet not one has been able to carry on my art.

sentences.zh: 吾之術，受於師者才十之三，其十之七，則授徒時被其非法相取之勢迫而得之於無意者也。

translations.literal: Of my art, only three-tenths came from my master; the remaining seven-tenths I gained without intending to, when teaching disciples and being forced by their unlawful attempts to seize openings.
translations.idiomatic: Of everything I know, only three parts in ten came from my master. The other seven I learned by accident—when my disciples tried to steal the art by force, and in resisting them I discovered what I had never been taught.

sentences.zh: 是故名師易求，佳徒難訪。

translations.literal: Thus a renowned master is easy to find, but a worthy disciple is hard to come by.
translations.idiomatic: A famous master is easy to find; a worthy disciple is not.

sentences.zh: 佳徒意在得師，以天下之大，求之無不如意者。

translations.literal: A worthy disciple seeks only a teacher; in so vast a world, such a one will always find what he seeks.
translations.idiomatic: A worthy disciple wants only a teacher, and in a world this wide he will always find one.

sentences.zh: 至名師求徒，雖遇高資妙質，足以授道，而非其志之所存，不能耐勞苦以要之永久，則百貢而百見卻矣。」

translations.literal: But when a renowned master seeks a disciple, even if he meets one of keen talent and fine quality, fully fit to receive the Way, if the disciple's heart is not set upon it and he cannot endure hardship to pursue it to the end, then though the master offers a hundred times, a hundred times he will be refused."
translations.idiomatic: When a master seeks a disciple, he may meet someone of keen talent and fine quality, fully fit to receive the art—but if the student's heart is not in it, if he cannot endure hardship and stay the course, then though the master offers himself a hundred times, a hundred times he will be turned away."

sentences.zh: 佩言與竹齋同時處揚州，後歸歙，不知所終。

translations.literal: Peiyan and Zhuzhai lived in Yangzhou at the same time; later he returned to She, and nothing more is known of his end.
translations.idiomatic: Peiyan and Zhuzhai were contemporaries in Yangzhou. Later Peiyan returned to She, and nothing further is known of his fate.

sentences.zh: 江之桐，字蘭崖，安徽和州人。

translations.literal: Jiang Zhitong, styled Lanya, was a native of Hezhou in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zhitong, styled Lanya, came from Hezhou in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 年十餘歲，傭於江寧賣餅家，嗜讀書，其主人異之。

translations.literal: At just over ten years of age, he was hired out to a cake-selling household in Jiangning. He loved to read, and his employer found this unusual.
translations.idiomatic: While still in his early teens he worked as a hired hand for a cake seller in Jiangning. He was always reading, and his employer thought this strange.

sentences.zh: 招至家，居之樓上數年，讀左傳、國語、戰國策、史記、漢書、三國志畢。

translations.literal: The master took him into his home and lodged him on an upper floor for several years, until he had finished reading the Zuo Commentary, Discourses of the States, Intrigues of the Warring States, Records of the Grand Historian, Book of Han, and Records of the Three Kingdoms.
translations.idiomatic: The master took him in and put him up on an upper floor for several years, until he had read through the Zuo Commentary, Discourses of the States, Intrigues of the Warring States, Records of the Grand Historian, Book of Han, and Records of the Three Kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 乃謝主人去，自設小肆於市。

translations.literal: He then thanked his host and left, setting up a small shop in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: He then thanked his host and left, opening a small shop in the market.

sentences.zh: 更習武藝，手​​臂刀矛，皆務實用，變通成法。

translations.literal: He next took up martial arts—hands, arms, sword, and spear—all practiced for practical use, adapting received forms with flexibility.
translations.idiomatic: He then took up the martial arts—hand techniques, arms, sword, and spear—training everything for practical use and adapting established forms as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 且讀書，且習藝，讀稍倦，則趫舉翕張，以作其氣。

translations.literal: He read and trained at once; when reading wearied him, he would leap and stretch, expanding and contracting his limbs to stir his vital energy.
translations.idiomatic: He read and trained in turn. When reading tired him, he would leap and stretch, flexing and extending his limbs to rouse his breath.

sentences.zh: 已而默坐，以凝其神，晝夜無間。

translations.literal: Then he would sit in silence to concentrate his spirit, without break day or night.
translations.idiomatic: Then he would sit in silence to fix his spirit, day and night without pause.

sentences.zh: 至百日乃睡，睡十餘日，復如之。

translations.literal: He would go a hundred days before sleeping, then sleep for ten-odd days, and resume the same regimen.
translations.idiomatic: He would stay awake a hundred days, sleep for ten or so, and begin again.

sentences.zh: 讀史善疑，質之儒生，往往無以答。

translations.literal: Reading history, he was quick to raise doubts; when he put them to Confucian scholars, they often had no answer.
translations.idiomatic: When he read history he was quick to doubt; he would press Confucian scholars with his questions, and they often could not answer.

sentences.zh: 其藝通綿長、俞刀、程棓、瓘嵋十八棍，多取洪門，敵硬鬥強，以急疾為用。

translations.literal: His skills encompassed Mianchang, Yu's blade, Cheng's staff, Guanmei's eighteen cudgels, and much from the Hong School—meeting hardness with strength, valuing speed above all.
translations.idiomatic: His arts included Mianchang, Yu's blade, Cheng's staff, Guanmei's eighteen cudgels, and much from the Hong School—meeting force with force, relying above all on speed.

sentences.zh: 复及陣圖、形勢、器械，皆有理解。

translations.literal: He also understood battle arrays, terrain and disposition, and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: He also had a grasp of battle formations, terrain and disposition, and the use of weapons.

sentences.zh: 年六十餘，始遇荊溪周濟。

translations.literal: Not until past sixty did he meet Zhou Ji of Jingxi.
translations.idiomatic: Not until he was past sixty did he meet Zhou Ji of Jingxi.

sentences.zh: 濟故績學，自負經世之略，通武藝，好談兵。

translations.literal: Zhou was a man of solid learning who prided himself on statecraft, was versed in martial arts, and loved to discourse on warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou was a scholar of wide learning who prided himself on statecraft, was versed in martial arts, and loved to talk of war.

sentences.zh: 與語大悅，延教其孫，三年而之桐卒。

translations.literal: Delighted in conversation with him, Zhou retained him to instruct his grandson; three years later Zhitong died.
translations.idiomatic: Greatly pleased in talking with him, Zhou kept him on to teach his grandson. Three years later Zhitong died.

sentences.zh: 濟之言曰：「兵事至危，非得練士能臨敵苦鬥曆三十刻，及選鋒一可當三者，雖上有致果之志，下有死長之心，遇強敵不能必克。

translations.literal: Zhou Ji said: "Warfare is peril in the extreme. Unless one has seasoned troops able to engage the enemy in bitter combat for thirty double-hours, and elite vanguard fighters each worth three ordinary men, then even if the commander above is resolute to achieve victory and the ranks below are ready to die for their officers, one cannot be certain of defeating a strong foe.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Ji said: "War is the utmost peril. Unless you have seasoned troops who can face the enemy in hard fighting for thirty ke, and picked vanguard men each worth three ordinary soldiers, then even if the commander above is bent on victory and the ranks below are ready to die for their officers, you cannot be sure of beating a strong foe.

sentences.zh: 以力為本，以技濟之，謂之練士；

translations.literal: Building on strength as foundation and supplementing with skill—such men are called seasoned troops;
translations.idiomatic: Troops grounded in strength and sharpened by skill—those are seasoned troops;

sentences.zh: 作其勇者，謂之選鋒。

translations.literal: Those whose courage is cultivated to the highest pitch are called elite vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Men whose courage is forged to the highest pitch—those are the picked vanguard.

sentences.zh: 世之便騎射、習火器，以為士卒程，事取捷速，恆不能持久。

translations.literal: The world nowadays favors horsemanship, archery, and firearms as the standard for soldiers, seeking quick results—yet such men rarely endure.
translations.idiomatic: People today train soldiers in horsemanship, archery, and firearms, aiming for quick results—and such troops rarely last.

sentences.zh: 洎乎接刃，則霍然而去。

translations.literal: When blades meet at close quarters, they vanish in an instant.
translations.idiomatic: But when steel meets steel, they melt away.

sentences.zh: 故曰'巧不勝拙'。

translations.literal: Hence the saying, 'Cleverness cannot overcome plain stubbornness.'
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying: 'Skill cannot beat plain doggedness.'

sentences.zh: 若之桐，庶為知務。」

translations.literal: A man like Zhitong may be said to understand what truly matters."
translations.idiomatic: A man like Zhitong, one may say, understood what really counts."

sentences.zh: 梁九，順天人。

translations.literal: Liang Jiu was a native of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Jiu came from Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 自明末至清初，大內興造匠作，皆九董其役。

translations.literal: From the late Ming through the early Qing, all palace construction projects within the Forbidden City were supervised by Jiu.
translations.idiomatic: From the late Ming through the early Qing, all construction work in the inner palace was overseen by Jiu.

sentences.zh: 初，明時京師有工師馮巧者，董造宮殿，至崇禎間老矣。

translations.literal: At first, during the Ming there was a master craftsman in the capital named Feng Qiao, who oversaw palace construction; by the Chongzhen reign he had grown old.
translations.idiomatic: In the Ming there had been a master builder in the capital named Feng Qiao, who directed palace construction; by the Chongzhen reign he was old.

sentences.zh: 九往執業門下，數載，終不得其傳，而服事左右，不懈益恭。

translations.literal: Jiu went to study under him. For years he never received the full transmission, yet he served at Feng's side with unflagging, ever more respectful diligence.
translations.idiomatic: Jiu went to serve in his workshop. For years he never received the full art, yet he waited on Feng day after day with tireless, ever more reverent devotion.

sentences.zh: 一日九獨侍，巧顧曰：「子可教矣！」

translations.literal: One day Jiu alone was in attendance. Feng turned and said, "You may now be taught!"
translations.idiomatic: One day Jiu alone was in attendance. Feng looked back and said, "You may now be taught!"

sentences.zh: 於是盡授其奧。

translations.literal: Thereupon he imparted to him every secret of the art.
translations.idiomatic: With that he transmitted to him the whole of his craft.

sentences.zh: 巧死，九遂隸籍工部，代執營造之事。

translations.literal: When Feng died, Jiu was enrolled in the Ministry of Works and took over construction affairs in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: When Feng died, Jiu entered the rolls of the Ministry of Works and took over construction in his place.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十四年，重建太和殿，九手製木殿一區，以寸準尺，以尺準丈，大不逾數尺許，四阿重室，規模悉其，工作以之為準，無爽。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year of Kangxi, when the Hall of Supreme Harmony was rebuilt, Jiu personally crafted a wooden model of the hall. Using inches to calibrate feet and feet to calibrate rods, the whole was no more than a few feet across; its four slopes and layered chambers reproduced the design in full. The workmen took it as their standard, without the slightest deviation.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year of Kangxi, when the Hall of Supreme Harmony was rebuilt, Jiu made a wooden model of the hall with his own hands. Inch calibrated foot, foot calibrated rod; the whole was only a few feet across, yet its four slopes and nested chambers reproduced the design exactly. The craftsmen took it as their standard, and not a measure was off.

sentences.zh: 張漣，字南垣，浙江秀水人，本籍江南華亭。

translations.literal: Zhang Lian, styled Nanyuan, was a native of Xiushui in Zhejiang, his registered domicile being Huating in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lian, styled Nanyuan, was from Xiushui in Zhejiang, though his registered domicile was Huating in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 少學畫，謁董其昌，通其法，用以疊石堆土為假山。

translations.literal: In youth he studied painting, paid his respects to Dong Qichang, mastered his methods, and applied them to stacking stone and piling earth into artificial mountains.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he studied painting and sought out Dong Qichang, mastering his methods and applying them to piling stone and earth into artificial mountains.

sentences.zh: 謂世之聚危石作洞壑者，氣象蹙促，由於不通畫理。

translations.literal: He held that those who piled perilous rocks into grottoes and ravines produced a cramped, constrained effect because they did not understand the principles of painting.
translations.idiomatic: He said that those who heaped dangerous rocks into caves and ravines made landscapes that felt cramped and pinched because they did not understand painting.

sentences.zh: 故漣所作，平岡小阪，陵阜陂纮​​，錯之以石，就其奔注起伏之勢，多得畫意，而石取易致，隨地材足，點綴飛動，變化無窮。

translations.literal: Therefore what Lian created were gentle mounds and low hills, ridges and embankments, set with stones according to the flow and rise of natural terrain, often capturing the spirit of landscape painting. The stones he used were easy to obtain and sufficient to hand; his embellishments were lively and in inexhaustible variation.
translations.idiomatic: What Lian built were gentle knolls and low hills, ridges and embankments, stones set according to the natural flow and fall of the land—often achieving the spirit of a painted landscape. The stone was easy to find and always at hand; his placements were lively, his transformations endless.

sentences.zh: 為之既久，土石草樹，咸識其性情，各得其用。

translations.literal: Pursuing this art for long, he came to know the character of every kind of earth, stone, grass, and tree, and put each to its proper use.
translations.idiomatic: After long practice he knew the nature of every kind of earth, stone, grass, and tree, and used each where it belonged.

sentences.zh: 創手之始，亂石林立，躊躕四顧，默識在心。

translations.literal: At the start of a project, with stones standing in disorder, he would hesitate and look all around, composing the whole in his mind.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning, with stones standing in disorder, he would pause and look all around, holding the whole design in his mind.

sentences.zh: 高坐與客談笑，但呼役夫，某樹下某石置某處，不假斧鑿而合。

translations.literal: Seated high, talking and laughing with guests, he would simply call to the laborers: "Place such-and-such a stone under such-and-such a tree in such-and-such a spot"—and the pieces fit together without need of axe or chisel.
translations.idiomatic: Seated above, talking and laughing with guests, he would only call to the workmen: put this stone under that tree, place that one here—and the pieces fit together without axe or chisel.

sentences.zh: 及成，結構天然，奇正罔不入妙。

translations.literal: When finished, the structure seemed utterly natural; regularity and surprise alike entered into perfection.
translations.idiomatic: When it was done, the structure seemed wholly natural; the regular and the unexpected alike were brought to perfection.

sentences.zh: 以其術游江以南數十年，大家名園，多出其手。

translations.literal: He traveled south of the Yangtze practicing his art for decades; many great houses and famous gardens were his handiwork.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled south of the Yangtze for decades, and many great estates and famous gardens were his work.

sentences.zh: 東至越，北至燕，多慕其名來請者，四子皆衣食其業。

translations.literal: From east in Yue to north in Yan, many who admired his reputation came to invite him; all four of his sons lived by this trade.
translations.idiomatic: From Yue in the east to Yan in the north, many who admired his name came to invite him, and all four of his sons lived by the same craft.

sentences.zh: 晚歲，大學士馮銓聘赴京師，以老辭，遣其仲子往。

translations.literal: In his later years the Grand Secretary Feng Quan invited him to the capital; pleading age, he sent his second son in his place.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years Grand Secretary Feng Quan invited him to the capital; pleading old age, he sent his second son instead.

sentences.zh: 康熙中，卒。

translations.literal: He died during the Kangxi reign.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the Kangxi reign.

sentences.zh: 後京師亦傳其法，有稱山石張者，世業百餘年未替。

translations.literal: Later his methods spread to the capital as well; there was one known as "Mountain-and-Stone Zhang," whose family trade endured for more than a century without decline.
translations.idiomatic: Later his methods spread to the capital too; there was one called Mountain-and-Stone Zhang, whose family kept the trade for more than a century without decline.

sentences.zh: 吳偉業、黃宗羲並為漣作傳，宗羲謂其「移山水畫法為石工，比元劉元之塑人物像，同為絕技」雲。

translations.literal: Both Wu Weiye and Huang Zongxi wrote biographies of Lian. Huang said that he "transferred the methods of landscape painting to the stoneworker's art—a supreme skill comparable to Liu Yuan of the Yuan, who sculpted human figures."
translations.idiomatic: Wu Weiye and Huang Zongxi both wrote biographies of Lian. Huang Zongxi said that he "moved the methods of landscape painting into stonework—a supreme art, comparable to Liu Yuan of the Yuan, who modeled human figures."

sentences.zh: 葉陶，字金城，江南青浦人，本籍新安。

translations.literal: Ye Tao, styled Jincheng, was a native of Qingpu in Jiangnan, his registered domicile being Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Tao, styled Jincheng, was from Qingpu in Jiangnan, though his registered domicile was Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 善畫山水，康熙中，祇候內廷。

translations.literal: Skilled in landscape painting, during Kangxi he served at the inner court.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at landscape painting and, in the Kangxi reign, attended the inner court.

sentences.zh: 奉敕作暢春園圖本稱旨，即命佐監造，園成，賜金馳驛歸。

translations.literal: Commanded to paint a design for the Changchun Garden, he pleased the emperor; he was immediately ordered to assist in supervising its construction. When the garden was complete, he was granted gold and sent home by express courier.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order he painted the design for the Changchun Garden and pleased the throne; he was at once appointed to help supervise its construction. When the garden was finished, he was given gold and sent home by express relay.

sentences.zh: 尋復召，卒於途。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned again, but died on the journey.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was summoned again, but died on the road.

sentences.zh: 劉源，字伴阮，河南祥符人，隸漢軍旗籍。

translations.literal: Liu Yuan, styled Banruan, was a native of Xiangfu in Henan and was registered in the Han Army Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan, styled Banruan, came from Xiangfu in Henan and was registered in the Han Army Banner.

sentences.zh: 康熙中，官刑部主事，供奉內廷，監督蕪湖、九江兩關，技巧絕倫。

translations.literal: During Kangxi he served as a principal secretary in the Ministry of Justice, attended the inner court, supervised the customs posts at Wuhu and Jiujiang, and was without peer in technical skill.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kangxi reign he served as a principal secretary in the Ministry of Justice, attended the inner court, and supervised the customs posts at Wuhu and Jiujiang. His technical skill was unmatched.

sentences.zh: 少工畫，曾繪唐凌煙閣功臣像，鐫刻行世，吳偉業贈詩紀之。

translations.literal: In youth he was adept at painting. He once painted portraits of the Tang ministers honored at Lingyan Pavilion, had them engraved and published; Wu Weiye composed a poem commemorating this.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was skilled at painting. He once painted the portraits of the Tang ministers at Lingyan Pavilion, had them carved and published, and Wu Weiye wrote a poem to commemorate the work.

sentences.zh: 及在內廷，於殿壁畫竹，風枝雨葉，極生動之致，為時所稱。

translations.literal: When serving at the inner court, he painted bamboo on palace walls—wind-stirred branches and rain-washed leaves of utmost vividness—widely praised in his day.
translations.idiomatic: At the inner court he painted bamboo on palace walls—wind-lifted branches and rain-beaten leaves rendered with extraordinary life—and was widely praised.

sentences.zh: 手製清煙墨，在「寥天一」、「青麟髓」之上。

translations.literal: He personally made "Clear Smoke" ink, superior even to "Vast Sky One" and "Blue Unicorn Marrow."
translations.idiomatic: He made Clear Smoke ink with his own hands, finer even than the celebrated Liaotianyi and Qinglinsui.

sentences.zh: 於一笏上刻滕王閣序、心經，字畫嶄然。

translations.literal: On a single ivory tablet he carved the Preface to the Pavilion of Prince Teng and the Heart Sutra—the characters sharp and distinct.
translations.idiomatic: On a single tablet he carved the Preface to the Pavilion of Prince Teng and the Heart Sutra, every character crisp and clear.

sentences.zh: 奉敕制太皇太后及皇貴妃寶範，撥蠟精絕。

translations.literal: By imperial command he cast seals for the Grand Empress Dowager and the Imperial Noble Consort; his lost-wax technique was consummate.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order he cast the seals of the Grand Empress Dowager and the Imperial Noble Consort; his lost-wax work was consummate.

sentences.zh: 時江西景德鎮開御窯，源呈赩樣數百種。

translations.literal: When the imperial kiln at Jingdezhen in Jiangxi was opened, Yuan submitted several hundred sample designs.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial kiln at Jingdezhen in Jiangxi was opened, Yuan submitted several hundred sample designs.

sentences.zh: 參古今之式，運以新意，備諸巧妙。

translations.literal: Drawing on forms ancient and modern, he infused new ideas and embodied every refinement.
translations.idiomatic: Drawing on forms old and new, he worked in fresh ideas and embodied every refinement.

sentences.zh: 於彩繪人物山水花鳥，尤各極其勝。

translations.literal: In overglaze figures, landscapes, flowers, and birds, each reached its highest excellence.
translations.idiomatic: In overglaze figures, landscapes, flowers, and birds, each kind reached its highest excellence.

sentences.zh: 及成，其精美過於明代諸窯。

translations.literal: When complete, their fineness surpassed all Ming imperial kilns.
translations.idiomatic: When they were finished, their fineness surpassed anything from the Ming imperial kilns.

sentences.zh: 其他御用木漆器物，亦多出監作，聖祖甚眷遇之。

translations.literal: Other imperial objects in wood and lacquer were also largely overseen by him; the Shengzu held him in high favor.
translations.idiomatic: Other imperial objects in wood and lacquer were also largely made under his supervision, and the Shengzu treated him with exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 及卒，無子，命官奠茶酒，侍衛護柩，馳驛歸葬，恩禮特異焉。

translations.literal: When he died without sons, officials were ordered to offer libations, guards escorted his coffin, and an express relay bore him home for burial—honors altogether exceptional.
translations.idiomatic: When he died without heirs, officials were ordered to offer libations, guards escorted his coffin, and an express relay carried him home for burial—honors altogether out of the ordinary.

sentences.zh: 唐英，字俊公，漢軍旗人。

translations.literal: Tang Ying, styled Jungong, was a Han Bannerman.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Ying, styled Jungong, was a Han Bannerman.

sentences.zh: 官內務府員外郎，直養心殿。

translations.literal: He served as an assistant director in the Imperial Household Department and was stationed at the Hall of Mental Cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: He served as an assistant director in the Imperial Household Department and attended duty at the Hall of Mental Cultivation.

sentences.zh: 雍正六年，命監江西景德鎮窯務，歷監粵海關、淮安關。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yongzheng he was ordered to supervise the kilns at Jingdezhen in Jiangxi, and also served as supervisor of the Guangdong Maritime Customs and the Huai'an Customs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yongzheng he was ordered to supervise the kilns at Jingdezhen in Jiangxi, and also oversaw the Guangdong Maritime Customs and the Huai'an Customs.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，調九江關，复監督窯務，先後在事十餘年。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianlong he was transferred to the Jiujiang Customs and again supervised the kilns, serving in all for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Qianlong he was transferred to the Jiujiang Customs and again supervised the kilns, serving in all for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 明以中官督造，後改巡道，督府佐司其事，清初因之。

translations.literal: Under the Ming, eunuchs supervised production; later this passed to circuit intendants, with provincial aides assisting—the early Qing followed the same arrangement.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Ming, eunuchs supervised manufacture; later the duty passed to circuit intendants, with provincial aides assisting—the early Qing kept the same system.

sentences.zh: 順治中，巡撫郎廷佐所督造，精美有名，世稱「郎窯」。

translations.literal: In Shunzhi, wares overseen by Governor Lang Tingzuo were famed for their beauty and were known in the world as "Lang ware."
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi, wares overseen by Governor Lang Tingzuo were famed for their beauty and were known as Lang ware.

sentences.zh: 其後御窯興工，每命工部或內務府司官往，專任其事。

translations.literal: Thereafter, whenever the imperial kiln went into operation, officials from the Ministry of Works or the Imperial Household were dispatched to take sole charge.
translations.idiomatic: After that, whenever the imperial kiln went into operation, officials from the Ministry of Works or the Imperial Household were sent to take sole charge.

sentences.zh: 年希堯曾奉使造器甚夥，世稱「年窯」。

translations.literal: Nian Xiyao once served on commission and produced ware in great quantity, known as "Nian ware."
translations.idiomatic: Nian Xiyao once served on commission and produced ware in great quantity, known as Nian ware.

sentences.zh: 英繼其後，任事最久，講求陶法，於泥土、釉料、坯胎、火候，具有心得，躬自指揮。

translations.literal: Ying succeeded them and held the post longest. He mastered ceramic technique—clay, glaze, body, and firing—with personal insight, directing operations himself.
translations.idiomatic: Ying came after them and held the post longest. He mastered ceramic technique—clay, glaze, body, and firing—through his own insight, and directed the work himself.

sentences.zh: 又能卹工慎帑，撰陶成紀事碑，備載經費、工匠解額，臚列諸色赩釉，仿古採今，凡五十七種。

translations.literal: He also cared for the workers and guarded the treasury, composing the Stele Record of Completed Ceramics, fully documenting expenditures and artisan quotas, and cataloguing fifty-seven varieties of colored glazes, drawing on antiquity and the present alike.
translations.idiomatic: He also cared for the workers and watched the treasury closely. He wrote the Stele Record of Completed Ceramics, setting down expenditures and artisan quotas in full and listing fifty-seven kinds of colored glazes, drawing on both antiquity and the present.

sentences.zh: 自宋大觀，明永樂、宣德、成化、嘉靖、萬曆諸官窯，及哥窯、定窯、均窯、龍泉窯、宜興窯、西洋、東洋諸器，皆有仿製。

translations.literal: From the Song Daguan ware through the Ming Yongle, Xuande, Chenghua, Jiajing, and Wanli official kilns, as well as Ge, Ding, Jun, Longquan, Yixing, Western, and Eastern wares—all were reproduced.
translations.idiomatic: From the Song Daguan ware through the Ming Yongle, Xuande, Chenghua, Jiajing, and Wanli official kilns, and from Ge, Ding, Jun, Longquan, and Yixing to Western and Eastern wares—everything was reproduced.

sentences.zh: 其釉色，有白粉青、大綠、米色、玫瑰紫、海棠紅、茄花紫、梅子青、騾肝、馬肺、天藍、霽紅、霽青、鱔魚黃、蛇皮綠​​、油綠、歐紅、歐藍、月白、翡翠、烏金、紫金諸種。

translations.literal: His glaze colors included pale powder-blue, deep green, rice-color, rose purple, crab-apple red, eggplant purple, plum green, mule-liver, horse-lung, sky blue, clear red, clear blue, eel yellow, serpent-skin green, oil green, Ou red, Ou blue, moon white, kingfisher, black gold, purple gold, and others.
translations.idiomatic: His glaze colors included pale powder-blue, deep green, rice-color, rose purple, crab-apple red, eggplant purple, plum green, mule-liver, horse-lung, sky blue, clear red, clear blue, eel yellow, serpent-skin green, oil green, Ou red, Ou blue, moon white, kingfisher, black gold, purple gold, and many more.

sentences.zh: 又有澆黃、澆紫、澆綠、填白、描金、青花、水墨、五彩、錐花、拱花、抹金、抹銀諸名。

translations.literal: There were also pour-yellow, pour-purple, pour-green, filled white, gold-tracery, underglaze blue, ink wash, five-color, incised design, embossed design, gilded wash, and silver wash, among other names.
translations.idiomatic: There were also pour-yellow, pour-purple, pour-green, filled white, gold-tracery, underglaze blue, ink wash, five-color, incised design, embossed design, gilded wash, and silver wash, among other styles.

sentences.zh: 奉敕編陶冶圖，為圖二十：曰採石製泥，曰淘煉泥土，曰煉灰配釉，曰製造匣缽，曰圓器修模，曰圓器拉坯，曰琢器做坯，曰採取青料，曰煉選青料，曰印坯乳料，曰圓器青花，曰制畫琢器，曰蘸釉吹釉，曰鏇坯挖足，曰成坯入窯，曰燒坯開窯，曰圓琢洋採，曰明爐暗爐，曰束草裝桶，曰祀神酬原。

translations.literal: By imperial command he compiled Illustrations of Ceramic Manufacture in twenty plates: quarrying stone and preparing clay; washing and refining clay; calcining ash and compounding glaze; making saggers; trimming molds for round ware; throwing round ware; shaping carved ware; gathering cobalt ore; refining cobalt ore; stamping bodies and grinding slip; underglaze blue on round ware; designing carved ware; dipping and blowing glaze; turning bases and trimming feet; loading greenware into the kiln; firing and opening the kiln; overglaze on round and carved ware; open and muffled kilns; binding straw for packing; and offering sacrifice to the gods in gratitude for success.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial command he compiled Illustrations of Ceramic Manufacture in twenty plates: quarrying stone and preparing clay; washing and refining clay; calcining ash and compounding glaze; making saggers; trimming molds for round ware; throwing round ware; shaping carved ware; gathering cobalt ore; refining cobalt ore; stamping bodies and grinding slip; underglaze blue on round ware; designing carved ware; dipping and blowing glaze; turning bases and trimming feet; loading greenware into the kiln; firing and opening the kiln; overglaze on round and carved ware; open and muffled kilns; binding straw for packing; and offering sacrifice to the gods in gratitude for success.

sentences.zh: 各附詳說，備著工作次第，後之治陶政者取法焉。

translations.literal: Each was accompanied by detailed explanation, setting forth the order of operations in full—later administrators of ceramic affairs took it as their model.
translations.idiomatic: Each plate had a detailed explanation, setting out the order of work in full; later administrators of ceramic affairs took it as their model.

sentences.zh: 英所造者，世稱「唐窯」。

translations.literal: Wares he produced were known in the world as "Tang ware."
translations.idiomatic: The wares he made were known as Tang ware.

sentences.zh: 戴梓，字文開，浙江錢塘人。

translations.literal: Dai Zi, styled Wenkai, was a native of Qiantang in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Zi, styled Wenkai, came from Qiantang in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 少有機悟，自製火器，能擊百步外。

translations.literal: From youth he was quick-witted. He made his own firearms capable of striking at a hundred paces.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was quick and inventive. He made his own firearms, able to hit a target a hundred paces away.

sentences.zh: 康熙初，耿精忠叛，犯浙江，康親王杰書南征，梓以布衣從軍，獻連珠火銃法。

translations.literal: In the early Kangxi reign, Geng Jingzhong rebelled and invaded Zhejiang. Prince Kang Jieshu marched south; Zi followed the army as a commoner and presented his method of the "linked-bead" musket.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Kangxi reign Geng Jingzhong rebelled and invaded Zhejiang. Prince Kang Jieshu marched south, and Zi followed the army as a commoner, presenting his method of the linked-bead musket.

sentences.zh: 下江山有功，授道員劄付。

translations.literal: For merit in taking Jiangshan, he was granted a dispatch appointing him a circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: For merit in taking Jiangshan he was granted a dispatch appointing him a circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 師還，聖祖召見，知其能文，試春日早朝詩，稱旨，授翰林院侍講。

translations.literal: When the army returned, the Shengzu summoned him. Learning that he could write, the emperor tested him with a poem on the spring morning court audience; pleased, he appointed him Hanlin Academician Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, the Shengzu summoned him. Learning that he could write, the emperor tested him with a poem on the spring morning audience; pleased, he appointed him Hanlin Academician Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 偕高士奇入直南書房，尋改直養心殿。

translations.literal: Together with Gao Shiqi he entered service in the Southern Library; soon he was reassigned to the Hall of Mental Cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Gao Shiqi he entered service in the Southern Library; soon he was reassigned to the Hall of Mental Cultivation.

sentences.zh: 梓通天文算法，預纂修律呂正義，與南懷仁及諸西洋人論不合，咸忌之。

translations.literal: Zi was versed in astronomy and mathematics and took part in compiling the Correct Meaning of Pitch Pipes and Calendar. He disagreed with Ferdinand Verbiest and the other Westerners, and all bore him ill will.
translations.idiomatic: Zi was versed in astronomy and mathematics and took part in compiling the Correct Meaning of Pitch Pipes and Calendar. He quarreled with Ferdinand Verbiest and the other Westerners, and they all resented him.

sentences.zh: 陳弘勳者，張獻忠養子，投誠得官，向梓索詐，互毆構訟。

translations.literal: One Chen Hongxun, an adopted son of Zhang Xianzhong who had surrendered and received office, tried to extort Zi; they came to blows and brought lawsuits against each other.
translations.idiomatic: One Chen Hongxun, an adopted son of Zhang Xianzhong who had surrendered and received office, tried to extort him; they fought and brought lawsuits against each other.

sentences.zh: 忌者中以蜚語，褫職，徙關東。

translations.literal: Those who envied him struck with slander; he was stripped of office and exiled to the Northeast.
translations.idiomatic: His enemies planted rumors against him; he was dismissed from office and banished to the Northeast.

sentences.zh: 後赦還家，留於鐵嶺，遂隸籍。

translations.literal: Later pardoned and allowed to return home, he remained at Tieling and was enrolled in the local registry.
translations.idiomatic: Later amnestied and permitted to go home, he settled in Tieling and took up residence there.

sentences.zh: 所造連珠銃，形如琵琶，火藥鉛丸，皆貯於銃脊，以機輪開閉。

translations.literal: The repeating firelock he made was shaped like a pipa; gunpowder and lead balls were all stored along the barrel's spine, opened and closed by a gear wheel.
translations.idiomatic: The repeating firelock he devised was shaped like a pipa lute; gunpowder and shot were stored along the barrel's spine and fed by a wheeled mechanism.

sentences.zh: 其機有二，相銜如牝牡，扳一機則火藥鉛丸自落筒中，第二機隨之並動，石激火出而銃發，凡二十八發乃重貯。

translations.literal: Its mechanism had two parts, interlocking like male and female; pulling one trigger let gunpowder and shot fall into the chamber, the second part moving in tandem; flint struck spark and the piece fired—twenty-eight rounds before reloading.
translations.idiomatic: Two interlocking mechanisms worked in sequence: pull one lever and powder and ball dropped into the bore; the second mechanism followed, flint struck steel, and the piece discharged—twenty-eight shots before it had to be reloaded.

sentences.zh: 法與西洋機關槍合，當時未通用，器藏於家，乾隆中猶存。

translations.literal: The principle matched the Western machine gun, though it was not widely adopted at the time; the weapon was kept at home and still survived in the Qianlong era.
translations.idiomatic: The design accorded with the Western machine gun, but it never came into general use; the weapon remained in his household and was still in existence as late as the Qianlong reign.

sentences.zh: 西洋人貢蟠腸鳥槍，梓奉命仿造，以十槍賚其使臣。

translations.literal: Westerners presented a coiled-gut air rifle as tribute; Dai was ordered to copy it and gave the envoy ten such guns as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: When Westerners presented a coiled-gut air rifle as tribute, Dai was commanded to reproduce it and sent ten copies back with the envoy as gifts.

sentences.zh: 又奉命造子母砲，母送子出墜而碎裂，如西洋炸砲，聖祖率諸臣親臨視之，錫名為「威遠將軍」，鐫制者職名於砲後。

translations.literal: He was also ordered to make a mother-and-child cannon: the shell was ejected from the mother barrel and burst on impact, like Western explosive artillery; the Kangxi Emperor led his ministers to inspect it in person, bestowed the name 'Weiyuan General,' and had the maker's official title engraved on the breech.
translations.idiomatic: He was also ordered to build a shell cannon whose projectile was launched from the parent tube and shattered on impact, like Western explosive ordnance. The Kangxi Emperor came in person with his ministers to witness the trial, named it the Weiyuan General, and had Dai's official title cut into the breech.

sentences.zh: 親征噶爾丹，用以破敵。

translations.literal: On the campaign against Galdan it was used to break the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: On the emperor's expedition against Galdan, it was deployed to smash the foe.

sentences.zh: 丁守存，字心齋，山東日照人。

translations.literal: Ding Shoucun, styled Xincai, was a native of Rizhao, Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Shoucun, courtesy name Xincai, came from Rizhao in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 道光十五年進士，授戶部主事，充軍機章京。

translations.literal: A jinshi of Daoguang 15, he was appointed a principal secretary in the Ministry of Revenue and served as a clerk on the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the fifteenth year of Daoguang, received appointment as a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue, and served on the Grand Council staff.

sentences.zh: 守存通天文、曆算、風角、壬遁之術，善製器。

translations.literal: Shoucun mastered astronomy, calendrical calculation, wind divination, and the arts of the Ren and Dun, and was skilled at making instruments.
translations.idiomatic: Shoucun was versed in astronomy, calendrical reckoning, wind divination, and the esoteric arts of Ren and Dun, and excelled at devising instruments.

sentences.zh: 時英吉利兵犯沿海數省，船砲之利，為中國所未有。

translations.literal: At that time English troops attacked several coastal provinces; the advantage of their ships and guns was something China had never known.
translations.idiomatic: English forces were then assailing several coastal provinces, and the superiority of their ships and cannon was unlike anything China had ever faced.

sentences.zh: 守存慨然講求製造，西學猶未通行，凡所謂力學、化學、光學、重學，皆無專書，覃思每與闇合。

translations.literal: Shoucun threw himself zealously into manufacturing; Western learning had not yet spread widely, and there were no specialized books on what were called mechanics, chemistry, optics, and gravitation—yet his deep thinking often coincided with them unawares.
translations.idiomatic: Shoucun threw himself into manufacturing with fierce resolve. Western learning had scarcely taken root; there were no dedicated texts on what would later be called mechanics, chemistry, optics, or gravitation—yet his long brooding often arrived at the same conclusions by intuition.

sentences.zh: 大學士卓秉恬薦之，命繕進圖說，偕郎中文康、徐有壬赴天津，監造地雷、火機等器，試之皆驗。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Zhuo Bingtian recommended him; he was ordered to submit illustrated explanations, and together with the bureau directors Wen Kang and Xu Youren went to Tianjin to supervise the manufacture of land mines, fire mechanisms, and similar devices—all proved successful in trials.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Zhuo Bingtian recommended him to the throne. He was ordered to prepare illustrated specifications and, together with the bureau directors Wen Kang and Xu Youren, went to Tianjin to oversee the production of land mines, ignition devices, and other weapons—all of which passed trial.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，從大學士賽尚阿赴廣西參軍事，會獲賊黨胡以暘，使招降其兄以晄，守存制一

translations.literal: In the early Xianfeng reign he followed Grand Secretary Saishanga to Guangxi as a military adviser; when a rebel named Hu Yiyang was captured, he was sent to induce his brother Yihuang to surrender; Shoucun devised a
translations.idiomatic: In the early Xianfeng reign he accompanied Grand Secretary Saishanga to Guangxi as a staff officer. When the rebel Hu Yiyang was taken, Shoucun was charged with winning over his brother Yihuang to surrender, and he devised a

sentences.zh: 匣曰手捧雷，偽若緘書其中，俾以晄致之賊酋，酋啟匣炸首死。

translations.literal: case called a 'hand-held thunder bomb,' made to look as though a sealed letter lay inside; Yihuang was made to deliver it to the rebel chief, who upon opening the case was blown to death.
translations.idiomatic: case he named the Hand-Held Thunder Bomb, disguised to look like a sealed letter inside; Yihuang was made to carry it to the rebel chieftain, who opened the case and was blown apart.

sentences.zh: 尋檻送賊渠洪大全還京，遷員外郎。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he escorted the rebel leader Hong Daquan back to the capital in a cage and was promoted to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after, he conveyed the rebel chieftain Hong Daquan to the capital in a cage and was promoted to vice director.

sentences.zh: 從尚書孫瑞珍赴山東治沂州團防，造石雷、石砲以御賊。

translations.literal: He accompanied Minister Sun Ruizhen to Shandong to organize militia defense in Yizhou, making stone thunder bombs and stone cannon to repel bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Minister Sun Ruizhen to Shandong to organize militia defenses at Yizhou, fashioning stone thunder bombs and stone cannon to hold bandits at bay.

sentences.zh: 尋調直隸襄辦團練，上戰守十六策。

translations.literal: Soon transferred to Zhili to assist with militia training, he submitted sixteen strategies for attack and defense.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Zhili to help organize local militias and submitted sixteen proposals on tactics of attack and defense.

sentences.zh: 十年，回山東，創議築堡日照要塞，曰濤雒。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he returned to Shandong and proposed building a fortified outpost at Rizhao called Taoluo.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he returned to Shandong and proposed erecting a fortified strongpoint at Rizhao, named Taoluo.

sentences.zh: 賊大舉來犯，發石砲，聲震山谷，賊辟易，相戒無犯。

translations.literal: When bandits came in force, he fired the stone cannon; the blast shook the valleys, the enemy fell back in fear, and they warned one another not to trespass.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits marched against him in strength, he fired the stone cannon; the roar shook the valleys, the enemy recoiled, and they warned one another never to come near.

sentences.zh: 丁家堡附近之民歸之，數年遂成​​都聚。

translations.literal: The people near Dingjiabu gathered under him, and within a few years it became a substantial settlement.
translations.idiomatic: People from the vicinity of Dingjiabu rallied to him, and within a few years the place grew into a thriving town.

sentences.zh: 同治初，復至直隸，留治廣平防務，築堡二百餘所。

translations.literal: In the early Tongzhi reign he returned to Zhili, remained to manage defense at Guangping, and built more than two hundred fortresses.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Tongzhi reign he went back to Zhili, stayed on to manage defenses at Guangping, and built more than two hundred fortified posts.

sentences.zh: 軍事竣，授湖北督糧道，署按察使。

translations.literal: When military affairs were concluded, he was appointed grain-intendant of Hubei and acted as provincial judge.
translations.idiomatic: When the military work was finished, he was appointed grain-intendant of Hubei and served as acting provincial judge.

sentences.zh: 充鄉試監試，創法，以竹筒引江水注闈中，時以為便。

translations.literal: As examiner for the provincial examinations he devised a method of channeling river water into the examination halls through bamboo pipes, which was then regarded as a great convenience.
translations.idiomatic: While supervising the provincial examinations, he invented a method of drawing river water into the examination compound through bamboo pipes—a practice widely praised at the time.

sentences.zh: 瀕江諸省，率仿行之。

translations.literal: Provinces along the Yangzi generally followed his example.
translations.idiomatic: Provinces along the Yangzi River soon copied his method.

sentences.zh: 尋罷歸。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was dismissed from office and went home.

sentences.zh: 所著書曰丙丁秘籥，進禦不傳於外；

translations.literal: His writings included the Secret Keys of Fire and Explosives, submitted to the throne and not circulated outside;
translations.idiomatic: Among his books was the Secret Keys of Fire and Explosives, presented to the throne and never released beyond the palace;

sentences.zh: 所傳者曰造化究原，曰新火器說。

translations.literal: Those that circulated were Origins of Natural Transformation and A New Treatise on Firearms.
translations.idiomatic: those that did circulate were Origins of Natural Transformation and A New Treatise on Firearms.

sentences.zh: 徐壽，字雪村，江蘇無錫人。

translations.literal: Xu Shou, styled Xuecun, was a native of Wuxi, Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shou, courtesy name Xuecun, was a native of Wuxi in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 生於僻鄉，幼孤，事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: Born in a remote village, orphaned young, he was known for filial devotion to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He was born in an out-of-the-way hamlet, lost his father while still a boy, and became known for devoted care of his mother.

sentences.zh: 性質直無華。

translations.literal: His nature was plain and unadorned.
translations.idiomatic: He was plain and unpretentious by nature.

sentences.zh: 道、咸間，東南兵事起，遂棄舉業，專研博物格致之學。

translations.literal: During the Daoguang and Xianfeng reigns, when war flared in the southeast, he abandoned the examination path and devoted himself to natural history and physical science.
translations.idiomatic: When fighting broke out across the southeast during the Daoguang and Xianfeng reigns, he gave up the civil-service examinations and devoted himself to natural history and the physical sciences.

sentences.zh: 時泰西學術流傳中國者，尚未昌明，試驗諸器絕鮮。
